old_entry.title: Game Boy Advance
old_entry.subtitle: Nintendo's Handheld Goes 32-Bit Without Losing the Past
old_entry.summary: Game Boy Advance widens the handheld, adds shoulder buttons and carries an existing cartridge library into a new generation.
body: The original Game Boy Advance launched in Japan on 21 March 2001. Its horizontal body places the screen between the controls, with L and R buttons on the shoulders. Nintendo paired a 32-bit processor with a reflective colour display. This AGB-001 hardware should not be confused with the later folding SP.

The cartridge slot accepted Game Boy and Game Boy Color software as well as new Advance games, subject to compatibility exceptions. Continuing an existing library gave the new machine a connection to its predecessors. New Advance cartridges were also physically smaller, making the change visible in the objects players carried.

A dedicated link cable could connect up to four systems for supported software. Some games allowed multiplayer from a single cartridge; others required one in every machine. That difference mattered when arranging a game with friends. The handheld's social possibilities depended on the particular software as well as the socket on its side.

The GBA's design featured a landscape form factor, diverging from the portrait layout of the previous Game Boy models. The design put the buttons to the sides of the device instead of below the screen. The shift was the work of French designer Gwénaël Nicolas and his Tokyo-based studio, Curiosity Inc.

Nintendo presents Game Boy Advance as a move from 8 to 32 bits, but the interesting part of the specification is how it translates into use. The 2.9-inch reflective display runs at 240 by 160 pixels and can show 32,000 colours, while the new L and R shoulder buttons expand the controls without cluttering the front. The machine's horizontal layout places the controls beside the screen and offers a different grip from the original Game Boy. This continuity supports genres that would have been harder to make readable on the older handheld: fast racing, strategy, richer animation and ambitious 2D conversions. The generational leap is presented as an expansion of the familiar everyday object Nintendo had established in 1989, rather than a break with it.

old_entry.title: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite
old_entry.subtitle: Portable Hunting Becomes a Social Ritual
old_entry.summary: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite makes a portable hunting party and continuity with an existing save part of its appeal.
body: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite expands Monster Hunter Freedom 2 with more quests, equipment and monsters. Built for PSP, it combines an extended solo adventure with cooperative hunts for nearby players.

Ad-hoc wireless play allowed nearby players to hunt together. Capcom emphasised this cooperative portable experience in its contemporary announcement. A difficult quarry gave the group a shared task, while the handheld hardware made meeting up with the other hunters part of arranging the session.

Save transfer from the preceding game let returning players carry progress forward rather than begin the expanded release empty-handed. By 24 April 2008, Capcom reported two million units shipped in Japan, twenty-nine days after release.

Monster Hunter Freedom Unite has more missions, equipment, and monsters than Monster Hunter Freedom 2, and a new Felyne fighter to help the player on their quests. Rarity 9 and 10 armor and weapons were added. Players can now hold up to 99 of each item type in their item boxes, store up to 20 equipment sets, and get ten equipment pages instead of six. A new type of quest, the "Epic Hunting Quest", was introduced, which enables the player to take on, one by one, up to four different monsters in one quest. Weapons can now have up to purple sharpness which is higher than white sharpness. The player can now accept HR 7-9 quests in the gathering hall and new elder quests outside the gathering hall from a Felyne beside the village elder. The downloadable content can give the player special armor for their Felyne along with early unlocks for some of the Felyne skills. The introduction of new monsters such as the Ukanlos have been put into the game with even more creatures than the last version of Monster Hunter Freedom 2 on the PSP system.
